headline: Apple Posts Record Q2 iPhone Shipments Amid Global Smartphone Market Downturn
summary: Despite a worldwide slump in smartphone sales, Apple has achieved its strongest-ever second quarter for iPhone shipments, according to new market data.
details: New reports from Omdia and Ars Technica indicate that Apple has defied the global smartphone market downturn, posting its best-ever second quarter for iPhone shipments.
This record performance comes at a time when the overall smartphone market is experiencing historic lows, largely attributed to a global memory chip shortage.
While many manufacturers are struggling, Apple's ability to maintain and even increase its market share highlights the resilience of its product ecosystem and consumer demand for its devices.
The data suggests that Apple's strategy and product lineup have resonated strongly with consumers, even in a challenging economic climate.

topic: microsoft tests streamlined windows search without ads
headline_marked: Microsoft tests [[Windows 11 search]] without ads and game recommendations
headline: Microsoft tests Windows 11 search without ads and game recommendations
summary: Microsoft is rolling out a cleaner Windows 11 search experience to Insiders, stripping out distracting tiles and prioritizing relevant results.
details: Microsoft is testing a streamlined version of the Windows 11 search menu, aiming to remove distracting elements and improve user trust. This update is currently available to Windows Insiders in the Experimental channel.
The revamped search homescreen will now display only recent searches, eliminating tiles that previously showed game recommendations, trending searches, and the 'image of the day'.
Web results are also being improved, with the search menu set to surface the 'most relevant answer' first, rather than prioritizing related products and promotions.

The updated search will offer clearer metadata and previews of files, making it easier to identify the source of search results. Results from local files, apps, and settings will be prioritized over web and Microsoft Store suggestions.

Testers can now disable web and Store recommendations entirely through the Settings menu. Microsoft also claims the new search system handles typos, extra letters, and partial words more effectively, alongside performance enhancements.
